sentences.text: CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE PRADEEP KUMAR SRIVASTAVA -----

For the Petitioner : Mr. Anmol Deepak, Advocate For the State : Mrs. Snehlika Bhagat, A.P.P. .....
Order No.05/ Dated:12.07.2024 1.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. The petitioner has been made an accused in connection with POCSO Case No. 137 of 2023 arising out of Mahila P.S. Case No. 30 of 2023, registered for the offence under Section 376(2)(L) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 4/6 of POCSO Act, pending in the court of learned Additional Judicial Commissioner-IV-cum-Spl. Judge, POCSO, Ranchi.

3. As per prosecution case, on 19.08.2023 at about 13:30 hrs, informant had stated that she had come to Ranchi from Latehar for studying in class 10th from one "Study Circle Coaching Institute,
Pandra" and currently she lives in a rented house in P.O.- Madhukam, P.S. Shukhdeo Nagar Thana,
Ranchi.

It has been alleged by the informant that one fine evening at around 6.00 p.m., when she was returning from her coaching institute, she came across with the accused who is the uncle of the informant and invited her to eat snacks with him near Galaxia Mall, Ratu Road, Ranchi.

It is also alleged that the accused has gifted her a cell phone alongwith a sim card, thereafter, the informant was taken upto room in the Ratu Road locality, where accused has allegedly raped with the informant.
The informant also alleged that she is a person with 40 % disability.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all as alleged in the FIR.
The petitioner is languishing in Judicial custody since 24.08.2023 without any rhymes and reasons.

Petitioner undertakes to co-operate in the trial of the case by remaining physically present as and when required and shall not indulge in any manner in tampering with the prosecution evidences or influencing the witnesses of prosecution, hence, the petitioner may be enlarged on bail.

5. Learned A.P.P appearing on behalf of State has opposed the prayer for bail of the petitioner and submitted that there are sufficient materials against the petitioner showing his involvement in the Kailash Oraon vs The State Of Jharkhand ......

present case, hence he does not deserve bail.
6. There is direct allegation against the petitioner of rape with the minor victim girl.
Trial has commenced and there are only four charge-sheet witnesses.
Learned trial court has asked for four months' time to conclude the trial.

7. Regard being had to the facts and circumstances of the case and nature of allegation coupled with materials available against petitioner, I am not inclined to release the petitioner, on bail, which stands rejected.

8. However, learned trial court is directed to conclude the trial within four months from the date of this order, otherwise the petitioner shall be at liberty to renew the prayer for bail, if trial is not concluded within aforesaid period.

(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) R.K/
